picks.headline: Starting protein evolution from AI-designed scaffolds beats nature
picks.excerpt: Broad Institute researchers found that starting laboratory protein evolution from AI-designed, more stable proteins beats starting from natural ones: an AI-designed scaffold gave a protease more room to acquire new mutations. They reprogrammed botulinum-neurotoxin proteases to target ataxin-2, achieving a 79-fold improvement over naturally derived versions. The result suggests generative protein design and directed evolution are complementary rather than competing tools for engineering therapeutic enzymes.
picks.rationale: Protein/bio pick: a concrete, actionable AI-x-bio method — AI-designed scaffolds as a better launchpad for directed evolution, with a hard 79x result. Distinct study and URL from prior Baker/protein-design and biomanufacturing cards.

picks.headline: AI weather emulators forecast subseasonal climate at 350x lower compute
picks.excerpt: NSF NCAR researchers are building AI weather-climate emulators such as CAMulator that reproduce complex atmospheric models at roughly 350x lower compute cost, enabling rapid subseasonal (2-8 week) forecasts. Once trained, the emulators generate long simulations in a fraction of the time supercomputer physics models require. The work targets the notoriously hard 2-8 week forecast gap between weather and seasonal climate prediction.
picks.rationale: Climate/weather pick: a 350x compute cut that reopens the hard 2-8 week subseasonal forecast gap; credible NCAR source and distinct from the ocean-circulation cards (07-26 AMOC, 07-22 GOFLOW).

picks.headline: Princeton's PPPL builds an AI to autonomously run fusion-heating gyrotrons
picks.excerpt: Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory will lead a Genesis Mission project to build an AI system that autonomously operates the gyrotrons used to heat fusion plasmas, alongside virtual simulations of the hardware. The effort is part of a US national initiative to harness AI for fusion-energy scientific discovery. Autonomous control of heating hardware is a step toward AI-managed operation of future fusion reactors.
picks.rationale: Fusion/physics-energy pick: AI as an autonomous operator of real fusion-heating hardware, a concrete AI-for-science control problem from a top-tier lab. Adds outlet diversity beyond phys.org.

picks.headline: Closed-loop AI 'self-driving lab' could cut clean-energy materials search by years
picks.excerpt: Tohoku University researchers built an AI-driven framework that fuses materials databases, machine-learning interatomic potentials, large language models, intelligent AI agents and automated experiments into a continuous feedback loop they call the '4th+ paradigm.' Experimental results feed back to refine AI predictions iteratively, dramatically cutting the time needed to discover advanced energy materials. The self-driving-lab approach targets longstanding trial-and-error bottlenecks in materials science.
picks.rationale: Materials-science pick: a full closed-loop 'self-driving lab' that wires LLMs, agents and automated experiments into one feedback loop — a distinct method story from prior screening-only materials cards (oled-ai, hiddenvars), and keeps outlets spread to a fourth source.

picks.headline: AI's black-box problem: physics discoveries no one fully understands
picks.excerpt: AI systems are accelerating physics discovery by finding hidden patterns in massive datasets, from particle detection at CERN to materials innovation at Argonne, yet the opacity of these models means researchers often get accurate results without understanding how the AI reached them. The article asks whether science is entering an era of 'discoveries without comprehension' and what that means for reproducibility and researcher training. It weighs the changing relationship between human physicists and increasingly autonomous AI systems.
picks.rationale: Meta/physics pick: a high-credibility Physics World synthesis on AI opacity in scientific discovery — directly relevant to how researchers should trust and train around AI. Fifth distinct outlet, distinct reflective angle rather than a single new result.
